summary: One confirmed Turkcell (TR) mail-sync sign-in appeared outside baseline for prof.kaya@aegean.edu (F2). Ten likely sign-ins came from Portugal via VPN vpn-edge-02 on LT-3104 (F3). Rejected: impossible travel (non-interactive token), password spray (shared egress), and KEV VPN relevance (unused or patched). No confirmed abuse chain; escalation required by evidence policy.

risk.rationale: No confirmed account takeover chain exists for prof.kaya@aegean.edu, so contain is not warranted. The only confirmed anomalous signal is F2: one sign-in from Turkcell (TR) outside the account's baseline ASN (T1078.004), but it is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not an interactive user sign-in, and the impossible-travel and password-spray narratives were rejected with valid critics. The PT sign-ins (F3) are explained by university VPN vpn-edge-02 from device LT-3104, and the KEV appliance claims are inapplicable or patched. Because the Turkcell mail-sync event remains outside baseline and is not fully explained as legitimate, it is a weak unexplained signal rather than a dismissed benign one; there are no data-quality conflicts requiring escalation.
